mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate slower economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5% in 1 month over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 declines for 2 consecutive quarters over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO rises > 1% in 1 month over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months signals a disinflationary environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as it reduces inflationary pressures and may prompt monetary easing.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL declines for 3 consecutive months over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% in a month and real final sales (RSAFS) also increase by more than 1% in the same month, it signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and economic activity improve.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 5% and RSAFS rises > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when HOUST rises > 5% and RSAFS rises > 1% in 1 month over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity and consumer spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS rises > 200,000 in 1 month over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it signals an accommodative monetary policy with inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL is rising over a 3-year rolling window.
